Safe 0x160c61636d3718b86979f8fba4f691f1f492acd5 on Ethereum Mainnet, nonce 97, Charter bafkreigg6ajqdb52kb644wcxegurt7r6jlclru4mjy3lwxkbh6avm3vgre. Disputed rule: R-4.6. The transaction is the batch of request 0xca4239c7925e35172ebec87941c76f61d50fdd57eef0b00d49a468ee040e1fcd, re-proposed after the Safe cancelled nonce 96. It delegatecalls MultiSendCallOnly 1.4.1 to approve the AllowanceHolder 0x0000000000001fF3684f28c67538d4D072C22734 for 500000000000 USDC base units. It then calls the AllowanceHolder's exec, which runs the Settler 0xaddC26a3854feaBFd20d6BF658254088D83a425A. The Settler pulls the USDC, sells it through Fluid, Curve and one unverified pool, and pays the buy token 0x085780639cc2cacd35e474e71f4d000e2405d8f6, which the Safe has held and approved before, to the Safe subject to a minimum output. The official 0x documentation lists the AllowanceHolder, deployed more than two years before the proposal, as the allowance target for Ethereum Mainnet. The official 0x deployments dashboard lists the Settler as the current Ethereum Settler. The transaction follows 0x's guidance to set allowances only on the AllowanceHolder, never on the Settler (docs.0x.org and contracts.0x.org, observed 2026-11-14). Both contracts have code verified on Sourcify, and Etherscan shows no security warning on either. Nine of the eleven addresses on the route had verified source before the proposal. The DENIED vote cited R-4.6 without naming a target or source. No admissible evidence supports a reasonable finding that any target is malicious, compromised, exploited, or high-risk (§ 3.7, § 3.8). Precedent 0x6eedd07c9fdd32f3245c45ea98e435154b6e7df90c2743f5cdae1a04452b6064 distinguished. Ruled secure.
